slides.lead: Every tool in this area is a variation on one pattern, which you met as Git LFS:
items: Compute a cryptographic hash of the file.
Store the file outside Git under that hash: content-addressed storage.
Commit a small pointer that records the hash and the size.
Tell Git to ignore the real file, or let a filter swap pointer and file.

slides.direction: The root-cause box of section 28.7, shown after the "two results, one commit" step.
slides.text:
Observed behavior : checking out the commit named by a run gives a different metric.
Git state         : the commit is intact. The run's working tree had a modified tracked file.
Mechanism         : "git rev-parse HEAD" names the last commit; it says nothing about the
                    index or the working tree. Python imported the files on disk.
Root cause        : the tracker recorded HEAD and not the difference between HEAD and what ran.
Why Git does this : a commit is a snapshot that was taken; uncommitted work is, by definition,
                    in no snapshot.
Correct fix       : if the patch was saved, apply it to the commit and rerun (Lab 33.3). If
                    not, the result cannot be reproduced; say so and rerun from a commit.
Prevention        : refuse tracked runs from a dirty tree, or record status and diff; treat
                    untracked files the same way.

slides.body: Five mistakes to watch for.

items: Recording only the commit ID of a run. Root cause: git rev-parse HEAD names the last commit and says nothing about the index, the working tree or untracked files.
Changing the data file and forgetting the pointer. Root cause: the data file is ignored, so Git does not watch it, and only the tool's verify step compares it with the pointer.
Treating the pointer as the backup. Root cause: the pointer identifies the bytes and cannot produce them; the store is a dependency that can be emptied.
Recording a model name, a registry alias or an image tag. Root cause: each is a mutable reference, like a branch, and can name something else tomorrow.
Ignoring the lock file because it is generated. Root cause: it cannot be regenerated identically from what is in Git, since the package index changes, so it is an input.

beats.text: Versioning by reference. You version a large file by committing a small file that names it by checksum, and by keeping the bytes in a store that is addressed by that checksum. A checksum is a fingerprint computed from every byte of a file. Identical bytes always give the same one, and one changed byte gives a different one.

beats.tele: Five mistakes to watch for.

beats.text: Recording only the commit ID of a run. Root cause: git rev-parse HEAD names the last commit and says nothing about the index, the working tree or untracked files.
beats.tele: Recording only the commit ID of a run. Root cause: `git rev-parse HEAD` names the last commit and says nothing about the index, the working tree or untracked files.

beats.text: Changing the data file and forgetting the pointer. Root cause: the data file is ignored, so Git does not watch it, and only the tool's verify step compares it with the pointer.
beats.tele: Changing the data file and forgetting the pointer. Root cause: the data file is ignored, so Git does not watch it, and only the tool's verify step compares it with the pointer.

beats.text: Treating the pointer as the backup. Root cause: the pointer identifies the bytes and cannot produce them; the store is a dependency that can be emptied.
beats.tele: Treating the pointer as the backup. Root cause: the pointer identifies the bytes and cannot produce them; the store is a dependency that can be emptied.

beats.text: Recording a model name, a registry alias or an image tag. Root cause: each is a mutable reference, like a branch, and can name something else tomorrow.
beats.tele: Recording a model name, a registry alias or an image tag. Root cause: each is a mutable reference, like a branch, and can name something else tomorrow.

beats.text: Ignoring the lock file because it is generated. Root cause: it cannot be regenerated identically from what is in Git, since the package index changes, so it is an input.
beats.tele: Ignoring the lock file because it is generated. Root cause: it cannot be regenerated identically from what is in Git, since the package index changes, so it is an input.

beats.text: Now, out of the lab. An evaluation team reports a ranking metric to a customer every quarter. A new engineer is asked to reproduce last quarter's number and cannot: the tracker names a commit, and the commit gives a different result.
beats.tele: Now, out of the lab. An evaluation team reports a ranking metric to a customer every quarter. A new engineer is asked to reproduce last quarter's number and cannot: the tracker names a commit, and the commit gives a different result.

beats.text: The lead goes down the table of identifiers in order. Code: the commit exists. The tracker has no dirty flag, so the state of the tree is unknown. Dependencies: the repository has a lock file, committed. Data: the path is recorded, not a checksum, and the file at that path has been replaced twice since.
beats.tele: The lead goes down the table of identifiers in order. Code: the commit exists. The tracker has no dirty flag, so the state of the tree is unknown. Dependencies: the repository has a lock file, committed. Data: the path is recorded, not a checksum, and the file at that path has been replaced twice since.

beats.text: Model: recorded as a registry alias, which has been promoted once since. Three of the rows were recorded as mutable references. The honest report to the customer is the one the root-cause box prescribes: the result can't be reproduced. Here's why. Here's the rerun from a commit with every identifier recorded.

beats.text: Answer out loud. The question asks for three things per cause: the cause, its place in an order, and its evidence. A strong answer uses the rows of the identifier table as its list, so that nothing is forgotten: code state beyond the commit, dependencies, environment, data, model, configuration.

beats.text: It justifies the order, for example by how cheap each test is and how often each cause occurs. For each cause it names the record or the command that would confirm or exclude it. And it says plainly what you report when the evidence needed for a cause was never recorded.

beats.text: A large file is versioned by committing a pointer that names it by checksum, with the bytes in a content-addressed store.
beats.tele: A large file is versioned by committing a pointer that names it by checksum, with the bytes in a content-addressed store.

beats.text: Git LFS, DVC and a hand-made pointer share hash, store and pointer; they differ in how the bytes follow when the pointer moves.
beats.tele: Git LFS, DVC and a hand-made pointer share hash, store and pointer; they differ in how the bytes follow when the pointer moves.

beats.text: The pointer and the file can disagree without Git noticing, and the store can be lost.
beats.tele: The pointer and the file can disagree without Git noticing, and the store can be lost.

beats.text: A run is identified by the commit, the dirty state and diff, untracked files, the data and model versions, the resolved configuration and the environment.
beats.tele: A run is identified by the commit, the dirty state and diff, untracked files, the data and model versions, the resolved configuration and the environment.

beats.text: Record immutable identifiers: full commit ID, lock file, image digest, data checksum, model version or hub commit hash, resolved configuration.
beats.tele: Record immutable identifiers: full commit ID, lock file, image digest, data checksum, model version or hub commit hash, resolved configuration.
